technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client and conventions already compatible with the Spring XD and Spring Cloud Stream codebases, rather than introducing a new service-discovery abstraction.

Implement module and admin registration through configurable Eureka client properties, with registration occurring during application startup and status updates reflecting the current lifecycle state.
Refactor the four named controllers to depend on an Admin SPI facade, with deployment-specific implementations selected through Spring configuration and dependency injection.
Expose module metrics through Spring Boot Actuator and Spring Integration channel-based mechanisms where appropriate, normalizing the result into a REST-facing metrics model.
Persist periodic metrics snapshots using the existing Redis infrastructure and a configurable export interval, defaulting to five seconds.
Port FTP functionality as source modules while preserving existing Spring XD module configuration and lifecycle conventions as far as the target repository permits.
Use repository-native CI configuration, assumed to be GitHub Actions, for build and test automation.
Build the module-launcher Docker image in CI and publish versioned images, plus an explicitly controlled default tag, to the springcloud DockerHub namespace.
assumptions: The increment is implemented by one developer and estimates represent active work-hours, excluding elapsed waiting time for reviews, credentials, or external approvals.
The existing repositories, build files, test infrastructure, and Spring XD/Spring Cloud Stream source code are available and buildable with moderate dependency fixes.
Eureka server infrastructure already exists or is available for integration testing; this estimate covers client registration and configuration, not implementing an Eureka server.
The existing module lifecycle provides identifiable states and callbacks that can be mapped to Eureka instance metadata or status without redesigning the lifecycle engine.
The existing Admin SPI contracts are sufficient to support the four controller refactorings; only adapter or implementation changes are required.

Metrics requirements are limited to capturing, normalizing, exposing, and persisting module metrics; no new metrics taxonomy, dashboard, alerting system, or long-term data-retention service is required.
Redis is available in development and test environments, and authentication, high availability, and production operations for Redis are out of scope.
The FTP modules can be ported from an accessible XD implementation without substantial licensing, protocol, or third-party dependency rework.
CI secrets, DockerHub permissions, and repository access are available before implementation and do not require organizational provisioning work.
Testing includes unit, integration, and representative end-to-end verification, but not performance, security certification, or multi-region deployment testing.
Documentation is limited to configuration, usage, migration notes, and CI/Docker publishing instructions.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing repositories, build system, module lifecycle, controller structure, SPI contracts, metrics facilities, Eureka configuration, and CI conventions; produce the implementation plan and identify compatibility constraints.

Implement module registration and state update behavior for module applications, including Eureka client configuration, startup registration, lifecycle state mapping, metadata, deregistration handling, and focused tests.
Configure and implement self-registration of the XD Admin server, including service identity, endpoint metadata, startup and shutdown behavior, configurable enablement, and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Controller refactoring to Admin SPI calls
activities.activity_description: Refactor ContainersController, StreamsController, ModulesController, and JobsController to invoke the appropriate Admin SPI implementation, preserve existing REST behavior, handle deployment-specific implementations, and update controller tests.

activities.activity_name: Direct module metrics capture and REST exposure
activities.activity_description: Explore and integrate the available Spring Integration channel and Spring Boot Actuator mechanisms, define a normalized module metrics representation, capture metrics directly from modules, expose them through REST APIs, and add unit and integration coverage.

Implement scheduled metrics export and persistence using Redis, including configurable five-second default interval, serialization and key design, error handling, retrieval support needed by REST APIs, and persistence tests.

Port the FTP source modules from XD into the SCS repository, adapt package structure and dependencies, preserve configuration and runtime behavior, register module metadata, and add representative module tests.

activities.activity_name: Continuous integration build and test setup
activities.activity_description: Create CI workflows for repository checkout, dependency resolution, compilation, unit tests, integration tests where supported, artifact collection, and failure reporting for incremental commits.

activities.activity_name: Module-launcher Docker build and publication workflow
activities.activity_description: Define or update the module-launcher Docker build, add CI image build and tagging logic, authenticate and publish to DockerHub, and verify image pull and startup behavior.

Run end-to-end scenarios covering Eureka discovery, Admin SPI controller operations, module metrics capture and persistence, FTP source usage, CI-produced artifacts, and representative deployment configurations; fix integration defects.
Document Eureka properties, module and Admin registration, metrics REST and Redis behavior, FTP module usage, CI prerequisites, DockerHub publishing, tags, and upgrade or migration considerations.

activities.activity_name: Final quality review and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Perform code review of the completed increment, clean up configuration and test fixtures, verify reproducible builds, run the final test suite, prepare release notes, and address final defects found during readiness checks.
